diagnostics.skewMarkedRight: Marked skewness (G1 = {g1}): the right tail (heavy birds) is longer.
diagnostics.skewMarkedLeft: Marked skewness (G1 = {g1}): the left tail (light birds) is longer.
diagnostics.heavyTails: Tails heavier than the normal (G2 = {g2}): there are more extreme birds than expected.
diagnostics.noOutliers: No weight flagged by the 1.5×IQR, 3×IQR, |Z|>3 or modified-Z (MAD) rules.
diagnostics.outlierCaveat: A flagged value is not necessarily an error: it may be a genuinely small or large bird. Check whether it was a weighing or typing error before deciding. Excluding here is temporary and only for comparison; it does not delete the data.

spc.notYetTitle: A control chart is not yet appropriate for this flock.
spc.notYetBody: There are {n} valid weigh-in(s) and at least {min} are required to estimate minimally reliable control limits (ideally 20+). With few subgroups the limits become so uncertain that they would produce false alarms or give false reassurance.
spc.notYetHint: In the meantime, the Trend tab shows how weight, CV and uniformity evolve, which is the correct reading with few weigh-ins.
spc.whyNotXbar: Raw mean weight is not charted: in growing birds the mean rises naturally and an X̄ chart would flag that trend as "out of control". What is monitored are quantities that stay approximately stable between weigh-ins: CV, uniformity and % deviation from the breed standard target. Each weigh-in is treated as an individual observation (I-MR chart).
spc.rule1: • Nelson rule 1: point {punto} outside the control limits ({valor}).
spc.rule2Above: • Nelson rule 2: nine consecutive points above the centre line (up to point {punto}).
spc.rule2Below: • Nelson rule 2: nine consecutive points below the centre line (up to point {punto}).
spc.rule3Up: • Nelson rule 3: six consecutive points steadily rising (up to point {punto}).
spc.rule3Down: • Nelson rule 3: six consecutive points steadily falling (up to point {punto}).
spc.signalNote: A signal indicates non-random variation worth investigating (feed, environment, health, weighing error); on its own it is not a diagnosis.
spc.noSignals: No signals from Nelson rules 1-3: the variation in {serie} between weigh-ins is compatible with random variation.

comparison.needTwo: At least 2 weigh-ins are needed to compare.
comparison.crossFlock: The weigh-ins belong to different flocks ({a} vs. {b}): the samples are <b2>independent</b2> by definition and Welch's t-test will be used.
comparison.crossLines: ⚠️ The genetic lines differ ({a} vs. {b}): a weight difference may be due to genetics rather than management.
comparison.designQuestion: How are the observations in the two weigh-ins related?
comparison.designIndependent: Independent: different birds in each weigh-in (e.g. two random samples, two flocks, two houses).
comparison.designPaired: Paired: the SAME birds weighed twice, recorded in the same order (bird 1 with bird 1, and so on).
comparison.designRepeats: Repeats of the same group: same flock on different dates, but without identifying individual birds.
comparison.unsureHelp: The choice matters: with paired birds the test analyses the individual differences (more powerful); with independent samples it compares the means of two different groups. If you weighed a random sample on each date without identifying birds, choose "Repeats of the same group".
comparison.pairedMismatch: For a paired test both weigh-ins must have the same number of birds in the same order (here: {a} vs. {b}).
comparison.titleWelch: Two-sample t-test (Welch, variances not assumed equal)
comparison.reject: At α = 0.05, there is statistical evidence of a difference between the two weigh-ins (p {p}).
comparison.notReject: At α = 0.05, no sufficient statistical evidence of a difference between the two weigh-ins was found (p {p}). This does not prove they are equal.
comparison.warnRepeats: ⚠️ As this is the same group measured twice without identifying birds, independence between samples is questionable: read the p-value as indicative, not conclusive.
comparison.warnSmall: ⚠️ At least one sample has n < 30: check normality and outliers before trusting the result.
comparison.needVariability: Both weigh-ins need at least 2 weights with variability.

datasetInference.twoSidedDesc: μ ≠ μ₀ — the mean differs from the value, in either direction

datasetInference.needMu0: Enter a hypothesized mean μ₀ to test the observed mean against that value.
datasetInference.needValues: At least 2 values with variability (non-zero standard deviation) are required.
datasetInference.reject: At α = {alfa}, H₀ is rejected: there is statistical evidence that the mean differs from {mu0} {unidad} in the stated direction (p {p}).
datasetInference.notReject: At α = {alfa}, H₀ is not rejected: there is not enough evidence to claim that the mean differs from {mu0} {unidad} (p {p}).
datasetInference.notRejectCaveat: Note: "not rejecting H₀" is not the same as "accepting H₀". It is not shown that the mean is exactly {mu0} {unidad}; only that the data provide insufficient evidence against it — which may also be due to a small sample.
datasetInference.warnVerySmall: • n < 10: the test depends heavily on the data being normal.
datasetInference.warnSmall: • n < 30: check normality and outliers before trusting the result.
datasetInference.warnSkew: • Markedly skewed distribution with a small sample.
datasetInference.warnIndependence: • The test assumes independent observations: review how the sample was obtained.

datasetComparison.title: Compare samplings
datasetComparison.needTwo: Save at least two samplings to be able to compare them across dates or flocks.
datasetComparison.designQuestion: How are the observations of the two samplings related?
datasetComparison.independentDesc: different units in each sampling (two dates, two flocks, two houses).
datasetComparison.pairedDesc: the SAME units measured twice, in the same order.
datasetComparison.repeated: Repeated measures of the same group
datasetComparison.repeatedDesc: same flock on different dates, without identifying units.
datasetComparison.unsureHelp: The choice matters: with paired observations the test analyses the individual differences (more powerful); with independent samples it compares the means of two different groups. If you took a fresh sample on each date without identifying the units, choose "Repeated measures of the same group".
datasetComparison.pairedMismatch: For a paired test both samplings must have the same number of observations in the same order (here: {a} vs. {b}).
datasetComparison.meansNote: If the error bars overlap widely, the difference between means is doubtful; the test's p-value is the formal criterion. The scale does not start at zero so as not to flatten small differences.
datasetComparison.categoriesTitle: Distribution by category (criterion of sampling A)
datasetComparison.deltaNote: Δ % is the change in B's proportion relative to A. It is descriptive: it is not a hypothesis test on the proportions.
datasetComparison.welchTest: Two-sample t-test (Welch, not assuming equal variances)
datasetComparison.reject: At α = 0.05, there is statistical evidence of a difference between the two samplings (p {p}).
datasetComparison.notReject: At α = 0.05, no sufficient evidence of a difference between the two samplings was found (p {p}). This does not prove that they are equal.
datasetComparison.repeatedWarning: ⚠️ Since this is the same group measured twice without identifying units, independence between samples is questionable: read the p-value as indicative only.
datasetComparison.smallSample: ⚠️ At least one sampling has n < 30: check normality and outliers before trusting the result.
datasetComparison.needVariability: Both samplings need at least 2 observations with variability.

aves.title: Uniformity Report — {variante}
aves.subtitle: Avimétrica Pro · Poultry weight, uniformity and performance analytics · Generated: {fecha} · v{version}
aves.normalityNotRun: Not assessed (≥3 weights with variability are required).
aves.normalOk: the normality hypothesis is not rejected: the data are compatible with a normal distribution (this does not prove it)
aves.normalRejected: the normality hypothesis is rejected: the weights depart from the normal distribution
aves.testsDisagree: ⚠️ The two tests disagree at 5%: borderline evidence; give priority to graphical inspection.
aves.k2Unreliable: ⚠️ With n < 20 the K² test is unreliable; give priority to graphical inspection.
aves.normalityNote: The tests do not replace graphical inspection (histogram and Q-Q plot in the application).
aves.outliersNone: No observation flagged by the 1.5×IQR, 3×IQR, |Z|>3 or modified-Z (MAD) rules.
aves.outliersNote: A flagged value is not necessarily an error: verify before excluding. No observation was removed in this analysis.
aves.tTestNotRun: Not run (an age with an available reference and n ≥ 2 with variability are required).
aves.tTestTitle: One-sample t-test against the target weight
aves.hypotheses: H₀: μ = {mu0} g · H₁: μ ≠ {mu0} g (two-sided, 95% confidence)
aves.tReject: At α = 0.05, there is statistical evidence that the flock's mean weight differs from the target of {mu0} g.
aves.tNotReject: At α = 0.05, no sufficient statistical evidence was found to conclude that the mean weight differs from the target of {mu0} g. This does not prove that they are equal.
aves.curveAlt: Distribution curve with the uniformity band
aves.histogramAlt: Histogram with an overlaid normal curve
aves.bandTitle: Distribution relative to the uniformity band
aves.bandAlt: Bar chart of the percentage of birds below, within and above the uniformity band
aves.bandNote: A {pct}% band around the observed mean ({min} – {max} g). It is a descriptive band of the flock's spread, not a confidence interval.
aves.targetTitle: Mean weight against the breed standard target
aves.targetAlt: Bar chart of the flock's mean weight with its confidence interval, against the target weight line
aves.targetNote: The error bar is the 95% CI of the observed mean. The target is drawn as a reference line because it is a breed guide value, not a measurement with its own uncertainty. If the line falls outside the interval, the difference from the target is statistically appreciable; the t-test below quantifies it. The scale does not start at zero.
aves.refWeights: Reference weights: management guides for the line
aves.refApproximate: APPROXIMATE values with no audited official guide
aves.localNote: The statistical calculations run locally with deterministic functions verified by automated tests.
aves.limSmall: The sample is small (n={n}): the estimates carry wide uncertainty and the tests have low power. Weighing at least 30 birds is recommended.
aves.limSamplingUnknown: The sampling method was not documented: if the birds were not selected at random, the results may not represent the whole flock.
aves.limSamplingConvenience: Sampling was by convenience: the birds that are easiest to catch may differ systematically from the rest of the flock (selection bias).
aves.limApproxLine: The reference weights for this genetic line are APPROXIMATE (no audited official guide): the comparison against the target is indicative.
aves.limNoAge: The flock's age was not given: it was not possible to compare against the genetic line's target weight.
aves.limNormality: The weights depart from the normal distribution: the theoretical probabilities and the t-test must be interpreted with caution (see histogram and Q-Q plot).
aves.limOutliers: {n} possible outlier(s) were detected, which influence the mean, SD and CV. Check whether they are measurement errors or genuine birds.
aves.limProfessional: This report describes the weigh-in analysed; it does not replace the judgement of the professional in charge of the flock.
aves.metodoIntro: All calculations are performed in grams with double precision; rounding happens only at presentation.
aves.metodoFVarianza: Sample variance: s² = Σ(xᵢ − x̄)² / (n − 1) · SD: s = √s²
aves.metodoBesselNote: n−1 is used (Bessel correction) because the weighing is a sample of the flock; the population version (÷n) only applies when the whole flock is weighed.
aves.metodoFEem: Standard error of the mean: SEM = s / √n
aves.metodoFIc: 95% CI for the mean: x̄ ± t₍₀.₉₇₅, n−1₎ · SEM
aves.metodoFUnif: Uniformity (±{pct}%): % of birds with weight in [x̄·(1−{low}), x̄·(1+{high})]
aves.metodoBandNote: The uniformity band describes the spread around the observed mean; it is NOT a confidence interval (a frequent conceptual error).
aves.metodoBandaIcAlt: Same-scale comparison between the uniformity band and the confidence interval of the mean
aves.metodoBandaIcNote: The two ranges, on the same axis and with the data of this flock, answer different questions: the ±{pct}% band tells between which weights most of the birds are; the 95% CI tells between which values the true flock mean plausibly lies. That is why the CI is much narrower, and narrows further as n grows, while the band does not: the band depends on how different the birds are, not on how many were weighed.
aves.metodoFTtest: One-sample t-test: t = (x̄ − μ₀) / SEM, with df = n − 1
aves.metodoPNote: Interpreting the p-value: the probability of observing a difference at least as large as the one seen, if H₀ were true. p ≥ α does not "accept" H₀; it only indicates insufficient evidence.
aves.metodoFPercentiles: Percentiles: linear interpolation, type R-7 (Hyndman & Fan, 1996)
aves.metodoFSkewKurt: Skewness G1 and kurtosis G2: adjusted estimators (Joanes & Gill, 1998) — those of Minitab/SPSS
aves.metodoFOutliers: Outliers: Tukey fences (1.5×IQR and 3×IQR), |Z| > 3 and modified Z with MAD > 3.5 (Iglewicz & Hoaglin, 1993)
aves.metodoBoxplotAlt: Box plot with the quartiles, the Tukey fences and the outliers
aves.metodoBoxplotNote: The box plot makes the already-tabulated position statistics visible: the box spans the central 50% (Q1 to Q3), the inner line is the median and the whiskers reach the most extreme data point within 1.5×IQR. The circles are the observations flagged as outliers — they are flagged, never removed automatically.
aves.metodoFNormalidad: Normality: Shapiro-Wilk (AS R94, Royston 1995) and D'Agostino-Pearson K² omnibus test (D'Agostino 1970; Anscombe & Glynn 1983)
aves.metodoQqAlt: Q-Q plot of the observed quantiles against the theoretical quantiles of a normal distribution
aves.metodoQqNote: Each point is one observation: its horizontal position is the weight expected under normality and its vertical position the weight actually measured. If the data were perfectly normal, all points would fall on the dashed line. Deviations at the extremes indicate heavier or lighter tails; a systematic curvature, skewness. This inspection is what no normality test can replace.
aves.metodoErr1: Confusing the ±{pct}% uniformity band with a confidence interval.
aves.metodoErr2: Using the population SD (÷n) with sample data.
aves.metodoErr3: Concluding "the means are equal" when p ≥ α.
aves.metodoErr4: Removing outliers without checking whether they are measurement errors or real birds.
aves.metodoErr5: Trusting a normality test without inspecting the histogram and the Q-Q plot.

pesajesComparison.designIndependent: Independent samples: different birds in each weigh-in.
pesajesComparison.designPaired: Paired samples: the same birds weighed twice, in the same order.
pesajesComparison.designRepeated: Repeated measures of the same group: same flock on different dates, without identifying birds. Independence between samples is questionable, so the p-value is indicative only.
pesajesComparison.linesDiffer: The genetic lines differ ({a} vs. {b}). A weight difference may be due to genetics rather than management.
pesajesComparison.meansAlt: Bar chart of the mean weight of both weigh-ins with error bars of the 95% confidence interval
pesajesComparison.meansNote: The error bars are the 95% CI of each mean. If they overlap widely, the difference is doubtful; the test's p-value is the formal criterion. The scale does not start at zero, so as not to flatten small differences: read the axis values, not just the relative height.
pesajesComparison.bandTitle: Distribution relative to the uniformity band
pesajesComparison.bandAlt: Grouped bar chart comparing the percentage of birds below, within and above the uniformity band in both weigh-ins
pesajesComparison.bandNote: The band is recomputed on the mean of EACH weigh-in, so it is a criterion of internal homogeneity, not a fixed weight range: two weigh-ins with different means have different bands. Δ % is descriptive and does not constitute a hypothesis test on proportions.
pesajesComparison.cvStable: Between A and B, the coefficient of variation did not change.
pesajesComparison.cvDown: Between A and B, the coefficient of variation fell by {delta} points.
pesajesComparison.cvUp: Between A and B, the coefficient of variation rose by {delta} points.
pesajesComparison.readingStable: The flock's homogeneity stayed stable between A and B: neither CV nor uniformity changed appreciably.
pesajesComparison.readingFavourable: The homogeneity indicators are favourable or stable: the flock did not become more uneven in B.
pesajesComparison.readingUnfavourable: The homogeneity indicators are unfavourable or stable: it is worth reviewing feeder, drinker, density and health status.
pesajesComparison.readingContradictory: The indicators contradict each other: one improved and the other worsened. It is worth reviewing the histogram of each weigh-in before concluding.
pesajesComparison.reject: At α = 0.05, there is statistical evidence of a difference in mean weight between the two weigh-ins (p {p}).
pesajesComparison.notReject: At α = 0.05, no sufficient evidence of a difference between the two weigh-ins was found (p {p}).
pesajesComparison.notRejectCaveat: This does not prove they are equal: it may be due to a small sample.
pesajesComparison.notRun: Not run: at least 2 birds with variability are required in both weigh-ins and, in the paired design, the same number of birds.
pesajesComparison.limCrossLot: The weigh-ins belong to different flocks: the differences may be due to the flock, the management or the age, not only to the factor being evaluated.
pesajesComparison.limAges: The ages differ ({a} vs. {b} weeks): in growing birds much of the weight difference is the normal expected growth, not an effect of management.
pesajesComparison.limSmallSample: At least one weigh-in has n < 30: check normality and outliers before trusting the result.
pesajesComparison.limIndependence: The test assumes independent observations within each weigh-in: review how the birds were selected.
pesajesComparison.limPractical: A statistically significant difference does not by itself imply zootechnical relevance: weigh the magnitude against the genetic line's target and the production context.
pesajesComparison.limProfessional: This report compares the samples analysed; it does not replace the judgement of the professional in charge of the flock.

evolution.weightAlt: Line chart of the flock's mean weight by date, compared with the breed standard target curve
evolution.noTargetCurve: The target curve is not shown because the age is missing in some weigh-in, or the genetic line has no reference for those ages.
evolution.homogeneityAlt: Line chart of uniformity and the coefficient of variation by date
evolution.homogeneityNote: Uniformity and CV read in opposite directions: a flock improves when uniformity rises and CV falls. Both are computed on the mean of EACH weigh-in, so they describe internal homogeneity, not closeness to the target.
evolution.gainAlt: Bar chart of the daily weight gain between consecutive weigh-ins
evolution.gainNote: The gain is computed between the MEANS of two weigh-ins, which are different samples of the flock and not the same birds followed over time. It is therefore an estimate subject to the sampling error of both weigh-ins: a low bar may reflect an unrepresentative sample rather than a real drop in growth.
evolution.trendUp: {etiqueta} rose by {delta} {unidad} between the first and the last weigh-in.
evolution.trendDown: {etiqueta} fell by {delta} {unidad} between the first and the last weigh-in.
evolution.homStable: The flock's homogeneity stayed stable over the period: neither CV nor uniformity changed appreciably.
evolution.homFavourable: The homogeneity indicators are favourable or stable: the flock did not become more uneven over the period.
evolution.homUnfavourable: The homogeneity indicators are unfavourable or stable: it is worth reviewing feeder and drinker space, density, environment and health status, as well as how the birds were selected in each sampling.
evolution.homContradictory: The indicators contradict each other: one improved and the other worsened. It is worth reviewing the histogram of each weigh-in, because a single extreme value can move the CV without altering uniformity, or vice versa.
evolution.lastOnTarget: At the last weigh-in the flock is practically on the genetic line's target.
evolution.lastAbove: At the last weigh-in the flock is {pct}% above the genetic line's target.
evolution.lastBelow: At the last weigh-in the flock is {pct}% below the genetic line's target.
evolution.limSampling: Each point is a different sample of the flock, not a follow-up of the same birds: the variations between dates include sampling error as well as real change.
evolution.limTarget: The comparison against the target depends on the recorded age being correct and on the selected genetic line matching the flock.
evolution.limSmall: Some weigh-in has fewer than 30 birds: its estimates are especially imprecise and may distort the trend.
evolution.limProfessional: This report describes the weigh-ins recorded; it does not replace the judgement of the professional in charge of the flock.

dataset.categoriesAlt: Bar chart of the percentage of observations in each category
dataset.histogramAlt: Histogram with an overlaid normal curve
dataset.shapiroOk: normality is not rejected: the data are compatible with a normal distribution (this does not prove it)
dataset.shapiroRejected: normality is rejected: the data depart from the normal distribution
dataset.shapiroNote: The test does not replace graphical inspection of the histogram.
dataset.normalityNotRun: Not assessed (at least 3 values with variability are required).
dataset.outliersNone: No observation flagged by the 1.5×IQR, 3×IQR, |Z|>3 or modified-Z (MAD) rules.
dataset.outliersNote: A flagged value is not necessarily an error. No observation was removed in this analysis.
dataset.tReject: At α = 0.05, there is statistical evidence that the mean differs from {mu0} {unidad}.
dataset.tNotReject: At α = 0.05, no sufficient evidence was found to conclude that the mean differs from {mu0} {unidad}. This does not prove that they are equal.
dataset.limSmall: The sample is small (n={n}): the estimates carry wide uncertainty and the tests have low power.
dataset.limSampling: It was not documented how the units were selected: if it was not at random, the results may not represent the whole set.
dataset.limNormality: The data depart from the normal distribution: interpret tests that assume it with caution (see histogram).
dataset.limOutliers: {n} possible outlier(s) were detected, which influence the mean, standard deviation and CV. Check whether they are measurement errors or genuine values.
dataset.limProfessional: This report describes the sample analysed; it does not replace the judgement of the professional in charge.

comparison.title: Sampling comparison — {modulo}
comparison.designIndependent: Independent samples: different units in each sampling.
comparison.designPaired: Paired samples: the same units measured twice, in the same order.
comparison.designRepeated: Repeated measures of the same group: same flock on different dates, without identifying units. Independence between samples is questionable, so the p-value is indicative only.
comparison.meansAlt: Bar chart of the means of both samplings with 95% confidence interval error bars
comparison.meansNote: The error bars show the 95% CI of each mean. If they overlap widely, the difference is doubtful; the test's p-value is the formal criterion. The scale does not start at zero so as not to flatten small differences: read the axis values, not just the relative height.
comparison.categoriesAlt: Grouped bar chart comparing the percentage per category between both samplings
comparison.categoriesNote: The grading criterion of sampling A was applied to both samplings. Δ % is the change in B's proportion relative to A: it is descriptive and does not constitute a hypothesis test on proportions.
comparison.reject: At α = 0.05, there is statistical evidence of a difference between the two samplings (p {p}).
comparison.notReject: At α = 0.05, no sufficient evidence of a difference between the two samplings was found (p {p}).
comparison.notRejectCaveat: This does not prove that they are equal: it may be due to a small sample.
comparison.notRun: Not run: at least 2 observations with variability are required in both samplings, and in the paired design, an equal number of observations.
comparison.limSmallSample: At least one sampling has n < 30: check normality and outliers before trusting the result.
comparison.limIndependence: The test assumes independent observations within each sampling: review how the units were selected.
comparison.limPractical: A statistically significant difference does not, on its own, imply practical relevance: weigh the magnitude together with the production context.
comparison.limProfessional: This report compares the samples analysed; it does not replace the judgement of the professional in charge.

privacy.title: Privacy policy
privacy.summary: Avimétrica Pro does not collect, transmit or share any personal data. Everything you record lives only on your device.
privacy.storageBody: The flocks, weigh-ins, samplings and datasets you record are stored in your browser's or device's local storage (IndexedDB and localStorage). The application works offline and sends none of that information to any server: there is no server.
privacy.collectionBody: Nothing. The application requires no accounts or passwords, uses no analytics or advertising tools, installs no trackers and shares no information with third parties. The site is served as static files from GitHub Pages; GitHub may log technical accesses (like any web server) under its own policy.
privacy.permissionsBody: The application requests no device permissions: no camera, no location, no contacts, no microphone.
privacy.backupsBody: The “Data backup” section exports your data to a file on your device, under your control. That file is not uploaded anywhere; sharing it or not is your decision.
privacy.deletionBody: You can delete your data at any time from the application itself, by clearing the site's browsing data in your browser, or by uninstalling the application. There is no server copy to delete.
privacy.contactBody: Gustavo Alonso Ardón · Universidad Nacional de Agricultura, Catacamas, Olancho, Honduras · gardon@unag.edu.hn

interp.excellentBase: Uniformity {unif}%, CV {cv}%: a very homogeneous flock.
interp.excellentDentro: {pctDentro}% of the birds ({dentro}/{total}) are within the ±10% range ({promedio} g).
interp.excellentBroiler: The flock will reach market weight in a synchronized way, allowing efficient depletion.
interp.excellentProduccion: Most birds are at peak lay simultaneously, making nutritional management easier.
interp.excellentPrepostura: The birds will reach sexual maturity at the same time, synchronizing the onset of production.
interp.excellentCrecimiento: Growth is well controlled and the birds are progressing evenly.
interp.detalleFuera: {pctDentro}% in range, {debajo} birds below ({pctDebajo}%) and {encima} above ({pctEncima}%).
interp.regularSesgoBajo: Skew towards low weights: a significant group with insufficient intake or limited feeder access.
interp.regularSesgoAlto: Skew towards high weights: possible overfeeding of one section or unequal competition.
interp.regularSimetrica: Symmetric but spread-out distribution: general variability in intake and growth.
interp.poorBase: Uniformity {unif}%, CV {cv}%: worrying. Only {pctDentro}% in range.
interp.poorBroiler: Light birds will yield less, and heavy ones may suffer leg problems and mortality.
interp.poorProduccion: Many birds are not laying while others lay irregularly, wasting feed.
interp.poorPrepostura: Light birds will delay their sexual maturity, creating staggered, inefficient production.
interp.poorCrecimiento: Unevenness tends to worsen if not corrected. Small birds will not catch up with the large ones without intervention.

peso.sinReferencia: Measured average weight: {promedio} g. No reference is available for comparison.
peso.medido: Measured weight: {promedio} g. {linea} reference at {sem} wk: {optimo} g ({min}–{max} g).
peso.bajoOptimo: Deviation: {desv}%. Within range but below the optimum.
peso.sobreOptimo: Deviation: {desv}%. Within range but above the optimum.
peso.cercaOptimo: Deviation: {desv}%. Very close to the optimum.

alerta.sinReferencia: Age not specified or genetic line without a reference. Limited diagnosis.
alerta.pesoMuyBajo: Very low weight: {deficit} g ({pct}%) below the standard. Verify the age ({sem} wk) and review feeding.
alerta.sobrepesoBroiler: Overweight: {exceso} g ({pct}%) above the optimum. May cause leg problems, ascites and mortality.
alerta.sobrepesoPonedora: Overweight: {exceso} g ({pct}%) above the optimum. Reduces feed conversion efficiency and may cause prolapse.
alerta.cvExtremo: CV {cv}% is extremely high (>15%). Suggests serious management problems, mixed ages or data errors.
alerta.cvAltoPonedora: CV {cv}% is high for a layer (expected <8%). Check feed uniformity and feeder space.
alerta.todasDebajo: All out-of-range birds are below. Possible insufficient feeding or excessive density.
alerta.todasEncima: All out-of-range birds are above. Possible overfeeding or incorrect age.
alerta.pocasAves: Only {n} birds weighed. Recommended minimum: 30 birds (ideally 50-100) spread across the house.
alerta.produccionBaja: Low uniformity in production: unproductive birds are eating feed without laying eggs. A direct loss.
alerta.engordeFinalBajo: Low uniformity at finishing: light birds will need extra days, increasing cost per kg produced.

causa.nutricionCalibrada: Nutritional program well calibrated for the line and age.
causa.competenciaDesigual: Unequal competition for feeder and drinker access.
causa.consumoInsuficiente: A subgroup with insufficient intake (submissive or sick birds).
causa.densidadExcesiva: Excessive density preventing uniform access to feed.
causa.consumoExcesivo: A subgroup with excessive intake due to an advantageous position in the house.
causa.variabilidadGeneral: General variability with no clear skew.
causa.cvMultifactor: CV >10% suggests multiple factors acting simultaneously.
causa.broilerTemperatura: Inadequate temperature in the first weeks (thermal stress).
causa.broilerTransicion: Poorly managed transition from starter to grower feed.
causa.broilerVentilacion: Inadequate ventilation with uneven comfort zones.
causa.crianzaMicroclimas: Microclimates from inadequate temperature or ventilation.
causa.crianzaBebederos: Drinkers with irregular flow limiting intake.
causa.preposturaTransicion: Late or premature transition to pre-lay feed.
causa.preposturaAsincronia: Asynchronous reproductive development due to maturity differences.
causa.preposturaComedero: Insufficient feeder space during the critical transition.
causa.produccionFases: Birds at different phases of the laying cycle.
causa.produccionMuda: Uncontrolled partial molt creating groups with different weights.
causa.produccionPicaje: Feather pecking causing stress and reducing intake in victimized birds.
causa.pesoBajoAgrava: Average weight below standard, worsening the unevenness.

rec.mantenerPrograma: Keep the current management program without abrupt changes.
rec.prepararNidadas: Prepare nests and lighting for the start of production.
rec.espacioComedero: Increase feeder space: at least 5 cm/bird (linear) or 1 pan/60 birds (automatic).
rec.accesoSimultaneo: Verify simultaneous access to feed during the first hours of light.
rec.separarLigeras: Separate light birds into a pen with extra feeder/drinker and reinforcement feed.
rec.ajustarRaciones: Assess whether the feeding program is overestimated. Adjust rations.
rec.verificarBebederos: Check drinker flow and pressure: water restriction reduces feed intake.
rec.broilerTemperatura: Uniform temperature: 33-35°C in week 1, decreasing 2-3°C per week.
rec.broilerCama: Check litter quality: excessive moisture favours infections.
rec.broilerPapel: Use paper on the litter for the first 3-5 days to ease access to feed.
rec.broilerDensidad: Density: do not exceed 30-35 kg/m² in heavy broilers.
rec.broilerIluminacion: Intermittent lighting (4L:2D) synchronizes meals and improves uniformity.
rec.broilerMolturacion: Check feed grinding: particles too fine or too coarse affect uniform intake.
rec.crianzaTemperatura: Check the temperature: small birds huddle in warm spots and do not eat.
rec.crianzaComedero: At least 1 cm/bird of feeder space in the first weeks.
rec.levanteRestriccion: Controlled feed restriction without compromising the lightest birds.
rec.levanteDesparasitar: Deworm if not done in the last 4 weeks.
rec.preposturaCalcio: Increase calcium gradually (transition to pre-lay feed).
rec.preposturaComedero: Increase feeder space before the onset of lay.
rec.preposturaIluminacion: Stimulating lighting (+15-30 min/week), uniform for the whole flock.
rec.preposturaClasificar: URGENT: Grade by weight and manage separately. Light birds: extra feed. Heavy birds: mild restriction.
rec.produccionZonas: If uniformity is <75%, manage by zones with specific diets.
rec.produccionMonitorear: Monitor individual production: out-of-range birds do not produce efficiently.
rec.produccionMuda: Consider induced molting to re-synchronize, or cull unproductive birds.
rec.pesoBajoEstandar: Weight {pct}% below standard. Increase energy/protein and rule out subclinical disease.
rec.pesoSobreEstandar: Weight {pct}% above standard. Reduce nutrient density or apply controlled restriction.
rec.repetirPesaje: Repeat the weighing in 3-5 days to assess the trend.

didactico.broilerInicio: Uniformity in the first week lays the foundation of growth. Every gram gained now multiplies 3-5× by the end of the cycle. Chick quality, temperature and access to water/feed are the three pillars of early uniformity.
didactico.broilerCrianza: In weeks 2-3 the broiler grows at its fastest rate. Birds that do not eat enough now will never reach market weight on time, wasting feed and housing days.
didactico.broilerEngorde: During grow-out, uniformity determines economic efficiency. A uniform flock allows depletion on a single date; an uneven one forces batches, increasing fixed costs per kg produced.
didactico.broilerEngordeFinal: At finishing, uniformity is the best indicator of profitability. Birds below = kg not produced; birds above = risk of ascites and leg injuries. Target: ≥85% uniformity.
didactico.ponedoraInicial: Uniformity in the first weeks predicts future performance. A flock at ≥85% by 6 weeks will have a higher, more sustained production peak. Birds that fall short in weight will have delayed reproductive development.
didactico.levante: Rearing (wk 7-16) is where uniformity most shapes the future. At least 80% is required for the birds to mature sexually at the same time. Light birds = small eggs and fewer eggs; heavy birds = overweight and prolapse.
didactico.prepostura: Pre-lay (wk 17-20) is the critical window: the reproductive system activates and weight must be in the optimal range. Uniformity ≥85% at 20 wk = a concentrated, high production peak; uneven = a low, drawn-out peak.
didactico.produccionAlta: Uniformity ≥85% in production means most birds are following their optimal laying curve, allowing diet and lighting to be tuned precisely for the whole flock.
didactico.produccionBaja: Low uniformity in production is very costly: light birds eat without laying; heavy birds lay eggs of variable quality. Every point below 80% can mean 2-3 fewer eggs per hen over the cycle. Early correction is essential.

media.que: The average weight of the {n} birds weighed, and how far the weights spread from that average.
media.formula: x̄ = Σxᵢ / n · s = √[ Σ(xᵢ − x̄)² / (n − 1) ]
media.interp: On average the birds weigh {mean} g and a "typical" bird deviates about {sd0} g from that average. We divide by n−1 ({nm1}) rather than n because a sample was weighed, not the whole flock: without that correction the spread would be underestimated.
media.err1: Using the population formula (÷n) with sample data.
media.err2: Comparing standard deviations of flocks with very different average weights without going through the CV.

cv.que: The spread expressed as a percentage of the mean, so flocks of different weights can be compared.
cv.interp: {cv}% means the spread equals {cv}% of the average weight. In poultry, a low CV (≈8% or less at many stages) indicates an even flock; the exact threshold depends on species, line and age.
cv.err1: Interpreting the CV without considering age: in the first week the natural CV is higher.
cv.err2: Confusing the CV (relative) with the SD (absolute, in grams).

unif.que: The percentage of birds whose weight falls within the band [x̄ − {pct}%, x̄ + {pct}%].
unif.resultado: {dentro} of {total} birds inside the band → uniformity = {unif}%.
unif.interp: It measures what share of the flock is "close" to the average. The traditional poultry criterion uses ±10%, and ≥85% is considered excellent in many guides; the chosen criterion must always be stated with the result.
unif.err1: Confusing the uniformity band with a confidence interval: the band describes the birds; the CI describes the uncertainty about the mean.
unif.err2: Comparing uniformities computed with different criteria (±5% vs. ±10%).

ic.que: The range of plausible values for the TRUE average weight of the whole flock, given that only a sample was weighed.
ic.interp: With 95% confidence, the procedure captures the true flock mean: if the sampling were repeated many times, 95% of the intervals built this way would contain it. It does not mean that 95% of the birds weigh between those values.
ic.err1: Reading the CI as a range of individual weights (that role belongs to the percentiles).
ic.err2: Claiming "there is a 95% probability that the mean is in this specific interval" — the confidence belongs to the procedure, not to one concrete interval.

ttest.que: Whether the difference between the observed average ({mean} g) and the line target ({mu0} g) can be explained by sampling chance.
ttest.interpReject: Since p < 0.05, the observed difference would be very unlikely if the flock truly averaged {mu0} g: there is evidence that the average weight differs from the target.
ttest.interpNotReject: Since p ≥ 0.05, the data cannot rule out that the true average is {mu0} g. Careful: this does NOT prove they are equal; power may be lacking (small sample).
ttest.err1: Saying "H₀ is accepted" or "the means are equal" when p ≥ α.
ttest.err2: Ignoring the assumptions: independent observations and approximate normality (critical with small n).
ttest.err3: Confusing statistical significance with zootechnical relevance: with large n, a few grams of difference can give a small p with no practical importance.

normal.que: Whether the shape of the weight distribution is compatible with a normal bell curve.
normal.formula: Shapiro-Wilk: W = (Σaᵢ·x₍ᵢ₎)² / Σ(xᵢ − x̄)² · D'Agostino-Pearson: K² = Z(g1)² + Z(g2)² ~ χ²(2)
normal.interpOk: Normality is not rejected: calculations that assume it (theoretical probabilities, t-test) are reasonable for these data.
normal.interpRejected: Normality is rejected: check the histogram and Q-Q plot for skewness, heavy tails or possible subpopulations before trusting calculations that assume normality.
normal.err1: Using the test alone without looking at the histogram and the Q-Q plot.
normal.err2: With large samples, trivial deviations give a significant p; with small samples, large deviations go unnoticed.
normal.err3: Shapiro-Wilk is powerful in small-to-medium samples; with very large n it almost always rejects — combine it with the size of the deviation, not just the p.

outliers.que: Observations unusually far from the rest ({n} flagged), by Tukey fences, |Z|>3 and the modified Z with MAD.
outliers.formula: fences: [Q1 − 1.5·IQR, Q3 + 1.5·IQR] · Z = (x − x̄)/s · Mᵢ = 0.6745(x − median)/MAD
outliers.interp: An outlier may be a typing/scale error or a genuinely different bird (sick, dominant). The decision to exclude belongs to the professional and must be documented; excluding without justification biases the results.
outliers.err1: Removing outliers automatically to "improve" the CV.
outliers.err2: Ignoring that the mean, SD and CV are sensitive to a single extreme value (the median and IQR are not).

converg.titulo: Convergence: observed uniformity vs. normal model
converg.que: Compare the actual count of birds inside the band ({unif}%) with the area the fitted normal (μ={mean}, σ={sd}) predicts between the same limits ({area}%). Same limits, different questions: what happened vs. what would happen under the model.
converg.formula: SE(p̂) = √[p(1−p)/n] · expected discrepancy (95%): ±1.96·SE · birds for ±ε agreement: n ≈ p(1−p)·(1.96/ε)²
converg.res1: Observed {unif}% vs. theoretical {area}%: a gap of {brecha} points.
converg.res2: With n = {n}, the discrepancy expected by chance is ±{margen} points, and uniformity can only move in steps of {salto} points (1/n).
converg.interpCompatible: The gap falls within the sampling margin: the normal model describes this flock well. For ±3-point agreement you would need ≈{nPara3} birds. Rule of thumb: with few birds a large gap proves nothing; with many birds, a small gap confirms everything.
converg.interpDesvio: The gap exceeds the sampling margin (±{margen} points): the difference is not explained by chance — the distribution deviates from the normal model. Review the histogram, Q-Q plot and normality tests; suspect skewness, outliers or subpopulations (e.g., mixed sexes).
converg.err1: Expecting exact agreement with small samples: uniformity is discrete (steps of 100/n) and sampling chance matters.
converg.err2: Believing that increasing n closes the gap if the flock is not normal: with non-normal data the gap becomes systematic — and that is a diagnosis, not a defect.
converg.err3: Confusing the two numbers: uniformity counts real birds; the area under the curve is a model prediction.
